events.title: Crusaders Assault Constantinople
events.description: The Fourth Crusade launched an assault on Constantinople, the great capital of the Byzantine Empire. The attack turned a crusade meant for the Holy Land against the Christian world's wealthiest city.
events.significance: The assault set in motion events that badly weakened the Byzantine Empire and deepened the rift between Eastern and Western Christendom.

events.title: Battle of Castillon Ends the Hundred Years' War
events.description: French forces defeated the English at Castillon in southwestern France. It was the last major battle of the Hundred Years' War.
events.significance: The victory effectively ended English ambitions to hold territory in France, and it marked a turning point in the use of field artillery.

events.title: Handel's Water Music Premieres on the Thames
events.description: As King George I sailed down the River Thames, a barge of about 50 musicians played George Frideric Handel's Water Music for the royal party.
events.significance: The suite became one of the best-loved works of the Baroque era and remains a staple of the concert repertoire.

events.title: Execution of the Romanov Family
events.description: Tsar Nicholas II, his wife, their five children and several retainers were executed by Bolshevik secret police at the Ipatiev House in Yekaterinburg, Russia.
events.significance: The killings ended the Romanov dynasty's three centuries of rule and became one of the most haunting episodes of the Russian Revolution.

events.title: The Spanish Civil War Begins
events.description: A military uprising against Spain's Republican government began, starting a conflict that would divide the nation for nearly three years.
events.significance: The war became a testing ground for the weapons and ideologies of World War II, and it led to Francisco Franco's long dictatorship.
